findings.problem: status is a freeform String instead of an enum typestate. Any string value ("", "deleted", "corrupted", or any future value) is structurally valid, so the compiler cannot enforce the domain lifecycle.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code may branch on unexpected status strings, silently mishandle shards, or produce corrupted lineage. Invalid state transitions are silently accepted at compile time.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with `pub status: ShardStatus` where `ShardStatus` is an enum with exactly the permitted lifecycle variants (e.g. `Pending`, `Validated`, `Sent`). Remove `is_sent` entirely.

findings.problem: Two independent bool flags `is_validated` and `is_sent` represent a 4-state Boolean cartesian product, but the domain only allows a subset (e.g. sent without validated is illegal). No invariant enforcement at the type level.
findings.failure_mode: The state {is_validated: false, is_sent: true} is constructable and represents an illegal lifecycle transition (shard sent before validation). No compile-time or runtime gate catches this.
findings.fix: Collapse `is_validated: bool` and `is_sent: bool` into a single `status: ShardStatus` enum typestate that encodes the legal transitions and makes illegal states unrepresentable.

findings.problem: `id` is a raw `String` with no domain constraints. Shard identifiers may have format, length, or uniqueness invariants that are entirely unenforced.
findings.failure_mode: Empty, malformed, or duplicate shard IDs are silently accepted. No type-level guarantee that ids are non-empty, properly formatted, or unique within a scope.
findings.fix: Introduce `pub id: ShardId` as a newtype struct wrapping `String` with a fallible constructor that validates format and non-emptiness, returning a domain error on invalid input.

findings.problem: `mark_sent` is a free function that mutates a struct by reassigning `status` to the literal string "sent" and setting `is_sent = true` separately. This dual-update is error-prone and the string literal "sent" is not connected to any type.
findings.failure_mode: If the string literal changes, or if a future developer adds another lifecycle stage, the dual-update pattern will drift. The function can be called on a shard that was never validated because the type offers no guard.
findings.fix: Replace with a method or constructor on the typed state machine: `ShardStatus::Sent::from_validated(validated_shard)` or similar, so the transition is only available from the correct preceding state.

findings.problem: No validation constructor on `ShardWorkflow`. The struct exposes all fields as `pub`, allowing callers to construct any invalid combination without a factory gate.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can `ShardWorkflow { id: "".into(), status: "".into(), is_validated: false, is_sent: true, sent_at_epoch_ms: None }` and the compiler will not complain.
findings.fix: Make all fields `pub(crate)` or private, and provide a single fallible constructor `ShardWorkflow::new(...)` that validates invariants and returns a typed domain error.

findings.problem: `mark_sent` creates a new String via `.to_string()` for the "sent" literal on every call, even though the value is a known constant.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation on every invocation. For a hot path this adds measurable latency and allocation pressure.
findings.fix: Use a `ShardStatus` enum (which is zero-cost, stack-only) instead of `String`. If a String must remain, use `&'static str` for constant status labels.

findings.problem: `mark_sent` performs a state mutation (`item.status = "sent".to_string()`) that mixes domain transition logic with imperative field assignment rather than expressing the transition as a pure function from one valid typestate to another.
findings.failure_mode: The mutation pattern makes it harder to reason about invariants and harder to test the pure transition logic independently of the struct layout.
findings.fix: Define `mark_sent` as a pure function that takes a validated `ShardWorkflow` and returns a new `ShardWorkflow` with the typed `ShardStatus::Sent`, or better yet, make it a method on the validated typestate variant.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for `mark_sent` or any lifecycle transition
no profiler data for allocation hot spots in the shard workflow pipeline
no allocation audit (no `try_reserve`, no allocation budget analysis)
no second-ring evidence (no fuzzing, property tests, or Kani proofs of state machine invariants)
no command-level evidence (no cargo test, cargo clippy, or cargo bench runs documented)
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate compiles but has fundamental type-level violations that make illegal shard states constructable at compile time. The dual bool flags and raw String status create a state space that exceeds the domain's legal transitions. Without enum typestates and a factory constructor, no amount of runtime testing can guarantee the invariant that sent shards were always validated. The missing evidence gates (benchmarks, allocation analysis, formal/state-machine proofs) leave performance and correctness claims unsubstantiated.
